title: Notation
body_md:
$[K]=\{1,\dots,K\}$; $S$ is the number of posterior
draws per datum when sampling is Monte Carlo.  Two ELBO-derived scalars
recur: the average rate $\bar R=\mathbb E_xD_{\mathrm{KL}}(q(\cdot\mid x)\Vert p)$ and the
average variational gap $\bar\Delta=\mathbb E_x[\log p(x)-\mathrm{ELBO}(x)]$; $\bar R$ is logged in every VAE run and $\bar\Delta$ wherever $\log p(x)$ is
tractable, and
Section~\ref{sec:certification} reads them as \emph{budgets}; an estimator
is \emph{licensed} when it is a certified upper bound on the quantity it
replaces (Section~\ref{sec:budgets}), and the certified quantity is the
\emph{estimand}.  For a configuration we write
$\mathcal A(C)=\mathcal A[\bar q_C]$, and we apply $\mathcal A$ to a joint
table where convenient, $\mathcal A(T)=\sum_iT(i,i)$, which is the same
functional in table coordinates.

label: thm:invisibility
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:invisibility}
\textbf{(I) One pair, whole package, shared data.}
For every $K\ge2$ there exist configurations $C^1,C^2$ with the same data
law and prior, differing only in encoder and decoder, with
$M(C^1)=M(C^2)$---every item of Definition~\ref{def:package}, per example
and in aggregate, to exact equality, including $p(x)$ as a
distribution---while $\mathcal A(C^1)=1$ and $\mathcal A(C^2)=0$.

\textbf{(I$'$) Moment blindness with a sharp threshold.}
For every $K\ge2$ and $m\ge2$ the pair in (I) can be built so that, in
addition: (N1) per-example posterior means are identical example by example,
so every functional of the means---per-dimension AU, their full covariance,
any statistic---coincides; (N2) every aggregate-posterior mixed moment of
degree below $m$ in the coordinates that $c_{\mathrm{dec}}$ reads coincides; (N3) the
threshold is sharp, with explicit degree-$m$ cross moments separating the
pair.  The blindness order $m$ is a design parameter independent of $K$.

\textbf{(II) Orbit form, for trained models.}
Every prior-preserving bimeasurable bijection $\tau$ of $\mathcal Z$ leaves
(m1)--(m3) and $I(x;z)$ exactly invariant for every $x$ (and per-dimension
AU when $\tau^{-1}$ acts as a translation on $\mathrm{supp}(\bar q)$), while
agreement transforms as $\mathcal A(C_\tau)=\bar q(\tau(\mathrm{Agr}))$; the full
statement and proof are in Appendix~\ref{app:orbit}.

name: Invisibility

label: thm:certification
title: Theorem
body_md:
\textbf{(a) Reconstruction side.}\label{thm:certification}
For any fixed measurable $E\subseteq\mathcal Z$,
$d_{\mathrm{bin}}\bigl(\bar q(E)\,\Vert\,\bar p_\theta(E)\bigr)\le\bar\Delta$;
with $E=\{c_{\mathrm{enc}}\nec_{\mathrm{dec}}\}$,
\[
d_{\mathrm{bin}}\bigl(1-\mathcal A_{q}\,\Vert\,\bar\eta_p\bigr)\;\le\;\bar\Delta ,
\]
and in fact $\bar\Delta$ decomposes as the sum of this binary-KL term, a Jensen
term, and a within-cell term, all non-negative.

\textbf{(b) Generative side.}
For the same event,
\[
d_{\mathrm{bin}}\bigl(\mathcal A_{q}\,\Vert\,\mathcal A_{\mathrm{prior}}\bigr)\;\le\;D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\bar q\Vert p)\;\le\;\bar R .
\]
head: environment
name: Two-sided certification

title: Proof
body_md:
Appendix~\ref{app:thm2}; (a) is the binary
specialization of the post-processing decomposition of the gap, (b) is
data processing plus the rate decomposition \citep{hoffman2016elbo}.

Part (a) certifies the posterior-sampling audit and part (b) the generative
one.  Inverting (b) at an observed $\mathcal A_{q}$ and a budget
$B\in\{D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\bar q\Vert p),\bar R\}$ yields a certified band
$\{a:d_{\mathrm{bin}}(\mathcal A_{q}\Vert a)\le B\}\ni\mathcal A_{\mathrm{prior}}$.  Its one-dimensional form loses nothing,
because by Theorem~\ref{thm:invisibility}(I) richer permutation-symmetric
summaries cannot flag the failure anyway.  All of its leverage comes from the
budget, whose price and floor are the subject of Section~\ref{sec:price}.

label: thm:price
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:price}
Write $\Lambda_Q=Q\Lambda Q^{\top}$.

\textbf{(a) Exact price and worst basis.}
$B_Q=\tfrac12\log\bigl[\det\mathrm{diag}(\Lambda_Q)/\det\Lambda_Q\bigr]$,
attained at $\mu^*=m_x$, $D^*_{ii}=1/(\Lambda_Q)_{ii}$.  Moreover
(i) $B_Q=0$ iff $\Lambda_Q$ is diagonal---exactly on the posterior
eigenbasis, up to axis permutations, signs, and within-eigenspace
rotations;
(ii) $\sup_Q B_Q=\tfrac d2\log\bigl(\mathrm{AM}(\lambda)/
\mathrm{GM}(\lambda)\bigr)$, finite and attained (Schur--Horn,
\citealp{marshall2011inequalities});
(iii) restricting the product family to Gaussians is without loss.

\textbf{(b) Estimand invariance under transport.}
For $R\in O(d)$, transport the configuration: $z\mapsto Rz$, decoder
$g'(w)=g(R^{\top}w)$, posterior $N(Rm_x,R\Sigma R^{\top})$, prior
$R_{\#}p$, and \emph{transported} maps $c'(w)=c(R^{\top}w)$.  Then the
joint law of $(c'_{\mathrm{enc}},c'_{\mathrm{dec}})$ under every
transported sampling law equals the original joint law; in particular
$\mathcal A_{q}$ under full-covariance posteriors, $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{prior}}$, and every functional of
code-pair laws are exactly invariant.

\textbf{(c) The asymmetry.}
For a fixed model, $Q\mapsto B_Q$ ranges over the closed interval
$\bigl[0,\tfrac d2\log(\mathrm{AM}/\mathrm{GM})\bigr]$ while every
transported estimand is constant; across models the price is unbounded
($\kappa\to\infty$).  A mean-field-budget certificate is a property of the
(model, basis) pair; the certified quantity is a property of the model.
Reporting a mean-field KL budget without its basis is ill-posed; the
price-minimizing basis is the posterior eigenbasis.  The declared code map is the
exact dual.  Theorem~\ref{thm:certification} holds for \emph{every} fixed
measurable pair $(c_{\mathrm{enc}},c_{\mathrm{dec}})$ at once, and a rate budget is a functional of
$\bar q$ alone, so changing the map moves the certified \emph{quantity} and leaves
the \emph{budget} fixed---the mirror of the basis, which moves the budget and
leaves the quantity fixed.  Agreement is a property of the (model, declared map)
pair and the budget a property of the model; reporting either without the other
is ill-posed, and Section~\ref{sec:exp-price} measures both halves on one
checkpoint.

\textbf{(d) Informative floor.}
Let $y\in[L]$ be any finite-alphabet label with $y\perp z\mid x$, and let
$\alpha$ be the held-out accuracy of any predictor of $y$ from the
\emph{sampled} code $c_{\mathrm{enc}}(z)$, $z\sim q(\cdot\mid x)$.  Then with
$h_2(\cdot)$ the binary entropy in nats and
$\gamma(\alpha)=H(y)-h_2(1-\alpha)-(1-\alpha)\log(L-1)$ (Fano's
inequality, \citealp{cover2006elements}),
\[
\bar R\;=\;D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\bar q\Vert p)+I(x;z)\;\ge\;I(x;z)\;\ge\;I(x;c_{\mathrm{enc}}(z))
\;\ge\;I(y;c_{\mathrm{enc}}(z))\;\ge\;\gamma(\alpha),
\]
and by Lemma~\ref{lem:width} every band
$\{a:d_{\mathrm{bin}}(\mathcal A\Vert a)\le B\}$ with $B\ge\gamma$ has width at least
$1-e^{-\gamma}$.  At $\gamma\ge1$ nat the width is $\ge1-e^{-1}\approx0.632$
regardless of the observed agreement.

\textbf{(e) Dataset floor.}  If the data law is empirical over $N$ points---the
same $N$ points that define $\bar q=\tfrac1N\sum_iq(\cdot\mid x_i)$ and
$\bar R$---then $I(x;z)\le H(x)=\log N$, so
$D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\bar q\Vert p)\ge\bar R-\log N$: \emph{every} licensed budget obeys
$B\ge\bar R-\log N$, the band has width at least $1-e^{-(\bar R-\log N)}$,
and certification at width $w^*$ is \textbf{impossible} whenever
$\bar R>\log N-\log(1-w^*)$---no estimator, however tight, can change this.

name: The coordinate price of certification

label: lem:width
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:width}
For $a\in[0,1)$ and $B>0$ let $W(a,B)$ be the width of
$\{x:d_{\mathrm{bin}}(a\Vert x)\le B\}$.  Then $W(a,B)\ge1-e^{-B}$, with equality iff
$a=0$.
head: environment
name: Width

label: lem:budgets
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:budgets}
Let $f$ be any measurable coarsening of $\mathcal Z$ and $\tilde q$ the
moment-matched Gaussian of $\bar q$.  Then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(f_{\#}\bar q\Vert f_{\#}p)\;\le\;D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\bar q\Vert p),\qquad
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\tilde q\Vert p)\;\le\;D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\bar q\Vert p)\ \text{when }p\text{ is Gaussian},
\]
so binned/grid plug-ins (data processing) and moment-matched Gaussian plug-ins
(maximum entropy at fixed moments) are \emph{lower} bounds and are not licensed
budgets.  By contrast $\bar R$ is licensed but loose by exactly $I(x;z)$; and
for any certified lower bound $\hat I\le I(x;z)$, $\;\bar R-\hat I$ is licensed.

name: Budget validity

label: lem:harmonic
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:harmonic}
Let $\mu_0$ be a distribution on $\mathbb R^2$ invariant under rotation by
$2\pi/m$, and $\mu_j=(R_{\theta_j})_{\#}\mu_0$ its rotations.  Then all
moment tensors of $\mu_j$ of total degree $t<m$ are independent of $j$; if
$\mathbb E_{\mu_0}[r^m e^{im\varphi}]\ne0$, the degree-$m$ tensors depend on $j$
through the phase $e^{im\theta_j}$.
head: environment
name: Harmonic blindness

title: Proof
body_md:
In polar form a degree-$t$ monomial moment is a linear combination of
circular harmonics $\mathbb E[r^te^{ik\varphi}]$ with $|k|\le t$ and
$k\equiv t\pmod2$.  Rotation by $\omega$ multiplies the $k$-th harmonic by
$e^{ik\omega}$; invariance of $\mu_0$ under $\omega=2\pi/m$ forces
$\mathbb E_{\mu_0}[r^te^{ik\varphi}]=0$ unless $m\mid k$.  For $t<m$ only $k=0$
survives, and $k=0$ harmonics are rotation-invariant, hence equal for all
$\mu_j$.  At $t=m$ the $k=\pm m$ harmonics survive and transform by
$e^{\pm im\theta_j}$.

title: Construction
body_md:
Take $\mathcal Z=\mathbb R^2\times\mathbb R^2$ with a product of uniform
annuli.  $c_{\mathrm{enc}}$ reads the coarse angular sector ($K$ of them) of plane
$\mathsf A$.  On plane $\mathsf B$, partition into $Km$ fine sectors and
let class $j$ be the union of the $m$ sectors congruent to $j$ mod
$K$---an $m$-fold rotationally symmetric set of zero mean; $c_{\mathrm{dec}}$ reads
the class.  The two configurations couple sectors to classes by the
identity and by the derangement $\sigma$, exactly as the grid couples rows
to columns.  The package items
repeat the grid computation verbatim, with joint cells
$O_{ij}=\text{sector}_{\mathsf A}(i)\times\text{class}_{\mathsf B}(j)$ (prior mass $1/K^2$
each; the cells are congruent, related by rotations of the two planes, so
rates and masses match).  For the new items:

label: prop:a4
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:a4}
For every probability vector $\nu$ with at least two positive entries there
exist coupled channels with index-wise identical encoder and decoder
marginals $\nu$ and exactly matched $I(c_{\mathrm{enc}};c_{\mathrm{dec}})$ whose agreements differ;
when $\max_i\nu_i\le\frac12$ the pair can be taken with $\mathcal A=0$ versus
$\mathcal A>\sum_i\nu_i^2$.  The feasible set of $\mathcal A$ over all
couplings with both marginals $\nu$ is exactly
$[\max(0,\,2\max_i\nu_i-1),\,1]$.
head: environment
name: Non-uniform marginals

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $x$ the pair (encoder pushforward, decoder pullback) is a change
of variables: reconstruction integrands compose to the original,
$D_{\mathrm{KL}}$ is invariant under bimeasurable bijections applied to both
arguments (prior preserved), so (m1)--(m3) are pointwise invariant, and
$I(x;z)$ is invariant as a functional of the joint law.  The aggregate
posterior transforms as $\bar q_\tau=\tau^{-1}_{\#}\bar q$, so
\[
\mathcal A(C_\tau)=\bar q_\tau(\mathrm{Agr})=\bar q(\tau(\mathrm{Agr})),
\]
which differs from $\mathcal A=\bar q(\mathrm{Agr})$ iff $\tau$ transports net
$\bar q$-mass across the boundary of $\mathrm{Agr}$.  (The orientation matters:
writing $\tau^{-1}(\mathrm{Agr})$ here is wrong, though undetectable when $\tau$
is an involution; the verification suite checks a non-involutive
quarter-shift.)  For AU: the latent of $C_\tau$ is $\tau^{-1}(z)$ with $z\sim q(\cdot\mid x)$,
so if $\tau^{-1}|_{\mathrm{supp}(\bar q)}$ is a translation, posterior means
shift by a constant and every
$\mathrm{Var}_x\mathbb E[z_k\mid x]$ is unchanged.  Without the hypothesis AU can
move: on the uniform prior on $[0,1)$, swapping $[0,\tfrac14)$ with
$[\tfrac14,\tfrac12)$ is prior-preserving and moves
$\mathrm{Var}_x\mathbb E[z\mid x]$ from $0.0625$ to $0.015625$ in a two-example
configuration for which all other items are invariant.  \hfill$\square$

label: prop:structure
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:structure}
For every $K\ge3$ there exist coupled channels with identical agreement,
identical uniform marginals on both sides, and exactly matched mutual
information (hence matched joint, conditional, and marginal entropies)
whose error structures differ qualitatively (cyclic/bijective versus
many-to-one); for $K\ge4$ a derangement family matches \emph{all}
permutation-invariant scalars while pairwise and cyclic confusion structure
still differ.
head: environment
name: Structure

title: Proof
body_md:
Feasible-point constructions.  For the upper endpoint,
$x_0=1-(1-a)e^{-B}\ge a$ gives
$d_{\mathrm{bin}}(a\Vert x_0)=a\log\frac{a}{x_0}+(1-a)B\le B$, so
$x_+\ge1-(1-a)e^{-B}$.  For the lower endpoint, $x_1=ae^{-B/a}\le a$ gives
$d_{\mathrm{bin}}(a\Vert x_1)=B+(1-a)\log\frac{1-a}{1-x_1}\le B$, so
$x_-\le ae^{-B/a}$.  Hence
$W\ge(1-e^{-B})+a(e^{-B}-e^{-B/a})\ge1-e^{-B}$ since $B/a\ge B$; the added
term is strictly positive for $a\in(0,1)$.  At $a=0$,
$d_{\mathrm{bin}}(0\Vert x)=-\log(1-x)$, so $x_+=1-e^{-B}$ and $x_-=0$ exactly.

label: lem:clip
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:clip}
Let $q_1,\dots,q_N$ be probability densities on $\mathcal Z$,
$\bar q=\frac1N\sum_i q_i$, and $T=\log q_i(z)-\log\bar q(z)$ with
$i\sim\mathrm{Unif}[N]$, $z\sim q_i$.  Then $T\le\log N$ almost surely,
$\mathbb E[T]=I(i;z)$, and for every $c>0$ the clipped statistic
$T_c=\max(T,-c)$ satisfies
\[
I(i;z)\;\le\;\mathbb E[T_c]\;\le\;I(i;z)+e^{-c}.
\]
head: environment
name: Clip tail

title: Proof
body_md:
$\bar q\ge q_i/N$ pointwise gives $T\le\log N$, and
$\mathbb E[T]=I(i;z)$ is the mixture form of mutual information.  Since
$T_c=T+(-c-T)_+$, the lower bound is immediate.  For the upper bound,
$\mathbb E[e^{-T}]=\frac1N\sum_i\int_{\{q_i>0\}}\bar q\le1$, so Markov's
inequality gives $\Pr(-T>u)=\Pr(e^{-T}>e^{u})\le e^{-u}$, and
\[
\mathbb E[(-c-T)_+]=\int_0^\infty\Pr(-T>c+s)\,ds\;\le\;\int_0^\infty
e^{-(c+s)}\,ds\;=\;e^{-c}.\qquad\square

label: lem:aq
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:aq}
Let $\hat{\mathcal A}_q$ average $S$ posterior draws at each of the $N$
test points, with independent noise for every (point, draw) pair, so that
it is the mean of $NS$ independent $\{0,1\}$-valued variables whose means
average to $\mathcal A_{q}$; then $C_q=[a_-,a_+]=\hat{\mathcal
A}_q\pm\sqrt{\ln(2/\delta_q)/(2NS)}$ contains $\mathcal A_{q}$ with probability
$\ge1-\delta_q$ (Hoeffding).  If $B\geD_{\mathrm{KL}}(\bar q\Vert p)$ with probability
$\ge1-\delta_B$, then
\[
U=\bigcup_{a\in C_q}\{b:d_{\mathrm{bin}}(a\Vert b)\le B\}=\bigl[\,b_-(a_-),\,b_+(a_+)\bigr],
\]
where $b_-(a)\le a\le b_+(a)$ are the two roots of $d_{\mathrm{bin}}(a\Vert b)=B$,
contains $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{prior}}$ with probability $\ge1-\delta_B-\delta_q$.
head: environment
name: Certifying with an estimated agreement

title: Proof
body_md:
On the event that $\mathcal A_{q}\in C_q$ and $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\bar q\Vert p)\le
B$, of probability $\ge1-\delta_B-\delta_q$ by a union bound,
Theorem~\ref{thm:certification}(b) gives $d_{\mathrm{bin}}(\mathcal A_{q}\Vert\mathcal A_{\mathrm{prior}})\le B$, so
$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{prior}}$ lies in the band at $a=\mathcal A_{q}\in C_q$ and hence in $U$.  Each band is
an interval containing $a$, and both of its endpoints are non-decreasing
in $a$: $\partial_ad_{\mathrm{bin}}(a\Vert b)=\log\frac{a(1-b)}{b(1-a)}$ has the
sign of $a-b$, so raising $a$ raises $d_{\mathrm{bin}}$ at every $b<a$ (the lower
root moves up) and lowers it at every $b>a$ (the upper root moves up);
hence the union of the bands over an interval of $a$ is the interval
stated.  \hfill$\square$
